description:
You are logged into OpenProject at http://localhost:8080 as admin (password: Admin1234!). You are a QA Analyst performing a critical defect triage session for the 'mobile-banking-app' project after a production incident.

Two bugs have been reported:
- 'Fix transaction history pagination bug' (currently New, assigned to alice.johnson) is now confirmed as a critical production issue affecting all users.
- The JWT token security audit ('Security audit - JWT token expiration', In progress, carol.williams) has uncovered that tokens are NOT being invalidated on logout, which is a security vulnerability.

Your tasks:
1. Change the priority of 'Fix transaction history pagination bug' to 'Immediate' (highest priority) since it's a production-affecting bug.
2. Change the status of 'Fix transaction history pagination bug' from 'New' to 'In progress' as the team is triaging it now.
3. Add a comment to 'Fix transaction history pagination bug': 'PRODUCTION INCIDENT: Users cannot see transactions older than 90 days. Customer support tickets increasing. Escalated to P0. All hands on deck until resolved.'
4. Change the priority of 'Security audit - JWT token expiration' to 'High' and add a comment: 'Security vulnerability confirmed: JWT tokens persist after logout. Must be patched before next release. Adding to Sprint 1 security hardening scope.'
5. Create a new work package of type 'Bug' in the 'mobile-banking-app' project with subject 'Emergency: Token invalidation on user logout' assigned to carol.williams in 'Sprint 1 - Auth & Onboarding', priority 'Urgent', with description 'Implement immediate token revocation when user logs out. Related to JWT security audit findings.'
6. Create a wiki page in the 'mobile-banking-app' project titled 'Incident Report - Transaction History' documenting the production incident including: the bug description, customer impact, escalation timeline, assigned team members, and remediation steps.

metadata.new_bug_subject: Emergency: Token invalidation on user logout
